# Andy Friday: advice for the first date

Summary of 13 videos and podcast episodes by [Andy Friday](https://www.youtube.com/@AndyFriday) (German-language YouTube dating coach), translated and condensed into English. Search used: <https://www.youtube.com/results?search_query=andy+friday+first+date>

**How this was made:** from the German auto-generated captions of each video, so quotes are my translation and some nuance is lost. Andy's opinions are his; some of the advice is contested, and I mark where he himself hedges. Where a video is a podcast, the co-host is his partner Jackie (Jacqueline).

**Important caveat about "second date" and "hand test":** I searched all 13 videos for the two pieces of advice you remembered. Neither exists in the exact form you described. What he *does* say on each topic is in [section 6](#6-your-two-questions-what-he-actually-says). Read that first if these are the points you care about.

## 1. Where to go: not a restaurant

*Source: [Erstes Date: Die besten Orte & Ideen](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=LfeehHEZ-YY)*

**His rule:** do something exciting and relaxed, and definitely not a restaurant. His favourite first date is a walk.

**Why a restaurant is bad**
- You sit stiffly opposite each other and keep thinking "what do I ask next?". The only stimulus is the other person, so any silence feels like a bad date.
- Time feels different. Three hours at one table is one repeated impression; 45 minutes of walking feels like "we experienced so much together".
- You cannot leave gracefully. On a walk you can say you need to go; at a table you must sit through the food.
- Ordering is awkward (salad means fiddling with the fork, a burger means jaw-lock and dripping sauce).
- The cinema is also bad: no talking, you sit stiffly side by side. *Example:* he once kissed a girl on the cheek in the cinema on an early meeting; she was shocked, saw them as friends and said "Andy, please never do that again". The relationship was not there yet.

**Why a walk works**
- You can move apart and together naturally. *Example:* "look, geese, can we feed them?" (two steps away), then come back shoulder to shoulder.
- Silence is normal, and there is always a new thing to comment on.
- It is daytime, among people, and either of you can leave.
- Same logic for anything you walk through: a museum or exhibition ("how do you see this picture?").

**His sample first date (Frankfurt):** meet at a landmark (the David statue); bring a six-pack of Radler; walk along the Main; sit at a café or with an Apfelwein; end on a picnic blanket. The point is that there is a journey and new things can happen. On the way: the love-lock bridge ("that could be us in 10 years"), geese with a straggling gosling, and a stag party with a shot tray (he either joins in or declines, either way he engages with what happens).

**Other ideas:** ice skating (funny if one of you cannot), paintball, laser tag (you see how the person reacts under tension, "more than comparing CVs"), escape room, mini-golf, an ice-cream date, jumping on a tourist bus in your own city. His most memorable date was an unplanned tour of a museum in Los Angeles where they played "secret agents". Shared adventure or role play creates a bond. He and Jackie would not do a sauna or thermal bath on date one, though some clients do.

**If you are stuck in a restaurant:** invent stories about the other guests ("those two in the back are on a date too, right?"). He says this works better from the 4th or 5th date.

## 2. Who pays

*Source: same video as above ([Erstes Date](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=LfeehHEZ-YY)); the money topic also appears in [NEVER ask these 6 questions, Part 2](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rIe72HD2rcM)*

- He and Jackie prefer going halves on a first date, or a small gesture: an ice cream or a drink. His rule of thumb: once it reaches double digits it is borderline; roughly 12 euros at most.
- **Why:** paying big creates an expectation ("you're the man, you pay") that carries to date two and three, and he does not want to "pay for her time". He wants to meet at eye level.
- **Why over-paying backfires** (Jackie's story): a man paid for all five dates at pricey places and she felt he expected something physical in return. Also, some women let the man pay and stay "hard to get", so he does not date those women.
- **The bill is also a test** (Part 2): does she just expect you to pay, or say "I'll take this round" / "next time is mine"? How she acts on date one predicts how she treats money in the relationship.
- Cultural note from him: Eastern Europe, the man pays; Germany, mixed; Scandinavia, women often pay first.

## 3. What to talk about

### 3.1 Go past facts: avoid the "job interview"

*Source: [Funkstille nach dem ersten Date? Mach das!](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=v1NaQ84u6qY)*

His main diagnosis of boring dates is that they stay at the *informational* level:

> "My sister works in insurance." / "I have an older brother." / "What does he do?" / "Footballer." / "Which league?"

Facts only, no values or emotion. Same for work: "I'm in controlling." "Which company?" "Do you like it?" "Quite." End of conversation.

**What to do instead:** move from information to the person. Ask why and how.
- *Example:* she says she is a vet, so ask "do you love animals?", "how did you come to that?". Then she tells a pet story, and you tell yours.
- **Get values through examples, not labels.** "Are you an honest person?" only gets "yes". Ask "when did you last lie or feel you had to?" and then why. Friendship: "How did you meet your best friend? What moment showed you that you can rely on her?"
- **Use figurative language, not summaries.** He says "I sat at my computer looking at the lonely green WhatsApp bubble, then closed the laptop and called other people" instead of "we drifted apart".
- **Talk about your passions,** even "boring" hobbies (gym, collecting old car mascots). The barrier is you mind-reading what she might think and censoring yourself, which dims your voice and eyes.
- **Don't perform.** Listen (he says he is present about 90% of the time) and, when you speak, share real things: fear, joy, hope. Drop the "I must convince her" agenda.
- **Why men avoid deep topics:** fear of negative topics (ex, lying, death). He calls this misplaced protectiveness: you decide for her what she can handle. She can always say "I don't want to talk about that".

### 3.2 Ask permission, then go deep in two minutes

*Source: [Die eine Frage, die beim 1. Date ALLES verändert!](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mKFwpaSk2uc)*

You can start a deep conversation after two minutes. The trick is to give her control first:

> "I'm not really a fan of small talk. I'd like to ask you a personal question if that's okay, but you don't have to answer if you don't want to."

She will usually be curious enough to say "okay, what?". Then ask:
- **"If everyone in this room were an identical clone of you, which character traits would still make you stand out?"** She starts to "sell herself" to you, which reverses the nice-guy trap of trying to convince her.
- **"When was the last time you cried?"** He asked this of 53 women after dates for a street video, always with the announcement first, and it felt comfortable.

**Eye contact:** don't stare. Give an impulse, hold contact, then release and look away, reconnect on the next impulse. That mix of pressure and release is the sexual tension.

### 3.3 The question game

*Sources: [Erstes Date](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=LfeehHEZ-YY) (rules) and [12 Fragen beim Ersten Date](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=usxEqvqAs7E) (list)*

Introduce it casually: "Do you know the question game?" (She will say no, or yes.) Four rules: (1) no boring questions; (2) back and forth, you ask one, I ask one; (3) you may not ask back the same question; (4) you start. Rule 3 is a trick: if you have something you do not want to answer, ask it of her, because she cannot return it. It also makes her wonder what secret you have.

**First question he suggests:** "When were you last really happy?"

**His favourite, after four or five rounds:** *"Do you actually find me attractive?"* Typical answer: "You're not quite my type, but..." and then she lists reasons. He says nobody among his participants reported a flat "no". It gives you confidence ("she likes me"), and then it is easier to take her hand or kiss her later.

**The 12-question list** (from the podcast; light-hearted, pitched as "I found a list of 12 questions, want to play?"). You can use all 12, 5 to 7, or write your own. Tip: give two answers, a first "honourable mention", then "but I'd like to give you another one" showing another side.
1. When were you last really happy?
2. What are you grateful for today?
3. Where would you like to travel next?
4. If you could time-travel, which year would you visit?
5. What is your favourite dish? (follow-up: "can you cook it?" then the flirty "then you can cook it for me sometime")
6. What do people only learn about you after a while?
7. What music do you like: favourite band, best concert?
8. What is the most embarrassing thing that happened to you that you can laugh about now?
9. Which historical epoch would you live in for a week, then come back?
10. What do you want someone who loves you to understand about you?
11. What is the best pick-up line anyone ever used on you? (He calls this very good from a man to a woman: you can then flirt via a third party, "that was a sexy line, he did it well. In his place I'd have been flattered too, you're a beautiful woman.")
12. If you could fly to space but had to stay a year, would you go?

**Innuendo:** he also shows a double-meaning line (telling his partner "you'd be a good slave, you take commands well") as a flirt element: playful, deliberately ambiguous. He does this with his long-time partner; he does not say how a first-date woman would react.

### 3.4 The six "taboo" topics

*Sources: [NEVER ask these 6 questions, Part 1](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=soLXA95Hx6w) and [Part 2](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rIe72HD2rcM). The video title is ironic: he says you *should* ask them.*

**Thesis:** society says exes, politics, religion (and money, what you are looking for, kids) are taboo on a first date. He says raise them on dates 1 to 3. A first date is a "demo version of a relationship": you want to see whether you fit, and whether you share a fighting culture. **"Postponed conflicts are doubled conflicts"**: they come back after 6 months, a year or 10 years. His wife's caveat, which he accepts: it is not an interrogation. You need not fire all six on date one, follow the feel of the date.

**The key technique is probing ("Nachhaken").** Differences show up at the 5th to 20th answer, not the first. A value such as "spontaneity matters to me" is a buzzword until you ask "give me an example". Listen to the stories.

| Topic | What to ask and watch for |
|---|---|
| **Exes** | How did it end, and what is the contact now? *Occasional* contact (a message once or twice a year) is fine and even a good sign. *Weekly* contact, or more messages than they send you, is a red flag. If every ex is "toxic, crazy", ask about the one before: at some point the common factor is them. Always 1 to 2-year relationships is an information point: it may mean they leave once the honeymoon ends. "I am how I am and won't change" is a note to watch in the first conflict. |
| **Politics** | Don't discuss party programs. Bring up something in the news, then say where you stand. What matters is *how* she handles a different opinion (tolerant, curious, or fixed), not what she votes. |
| **Religion** | Test openness plus concrete future: "Must the kids be baptised?" Probe: "And if your partner isn't Christian, would that be okay?" "It gives me support but I'd never insist" is fine; "of course my wife should be Catholic" is conflict potential. |
| **Money** | Number one reason for divorce filings, he says. Ask: "Do you invest? Do you put money aside? How do you see the roles regarding finances? How did you handle money in your last relationship?" Ask about background without judging: "did you get pocket money, when did you start working?" *Example:* two people both had no teenage job. One said "my father paid for everything", the other "I had a skiing accident at 13 and was barely mobile for two years, I badly wanted to deliver newspapers again". Same fact, very different worldview. Never merge accounts before marriage safeguards. |
| **What are you looking for?** | Ask "where are you relationship-wise, and what do you want now and long-term?" See his model answers in section 5.3. |
| **Kids (and marriage)** | Do you want them, why, when? Near a knock-out criterion. If one wants and the other does not, "maybe it will change" is hidden fear of losing her. He says a radical compromise on a core life plan fails. *Marriage example:* she says "someone I marry when it's the right one". Follow up: "What does right mean?" "My values." "Which ones?" "Loyalty." "An example of loyalty?" Keep going until it is concrete; otherwise the statement is a vacuum. |

**Why he pushes it hard:** he says his clients are far too conflict-avoidant, and many were surprised after 8 years by "another side" of their partner because they never went deep on the dates.

## 4. Physical contact, seating and the kiss

*Sources: [Körperkontakt beim Date](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=C5m_F1oojBs), [Frauen richtig anfassen](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mHsB9-T-0qU), [Funkstille nach dem ersten Date?](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=v1NaQ84u6qY), [Küss sie wie im Film](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZIK0YbOjVkw), [Woran du erkennst, dass SIE dich küssen will](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TTue4FWKKeU)*

### 4.1 Principles
- **Touch decides the outcome:** friends do not touch tenderly, so to get past "just friends" you must break that wall. If you wait until the goodbye, you face "should I kiss her now?" under maximum pressure, "and the train has already left".
- **"Desire arises in the hidden."** Keep early touches short. Build pressure, then give space: touch for a moment, then let go fully. The space is what makes her feel the attraction ("why did he take his hand away?").
- **Not too much, but not zero.** If she does not pull away, do not escalate: keep the same intensity. **If she flinches or withdraws her hand or foot, stop immediately.** *Cautionary example (Jackie):* on a "friendly" Korean barbecue that turned out to be a date, the man kept reaching for her hand and touched her foot under the table. She pulled back each time and sat "like a sailor's knot". He ignored it.
- People differ: some are very touchy, others get overwhelmed by a stranger. You cannot know on date one, so read the response.

### 4.2 Where to touch, in order (fine for date one, escalate gradually)
1. **Hands and forearm, first degree.** Handshake (not limp, not crushing), fist bump, high five, thumb wrestling ("come on, you're not strong enough", a playful tease). Forearm or upper arm: a *very* light touch with the back of the hand *while saying something*, e.g. "did you see the game yesterday?". Or brush off a bit of lint ("what have you got there?"). It should be "a breath of touch".
2. **Lower back**, gently, when guiding her through a door.
3. **Hug:** short (1-2-3), maybe one stroke of the back, then release. Common mistake: leaning in with hips a metre away, which reads as insecure. Stand straight and let hips touch (no grinding).
4. **Second degree**, only once there is a flirty vibe: footsie under the table, thigh (briefly, back of the hand first, check she still smiles, then maybe a second longer), a hair out of her face, whispering in her ear side by side. Do not go "from 0 to 100".

*Positive example (Jackie, their first date):* about an hour in, at the ice-cream shop, he held the door and briefly touched her upper arm. "I thought, apparently he's interested."

### 4.3 The trick: two communication channels
Level 1 is what you say, level 2 is touch. If you talk while you touch, she barely registers the touch. *Example:* say "with some people I can't open up so fast, but with you I feel I can" while taking her hand. Everyday practice: each time you have a new thought in any conversation, lightly tap the person's arm ("oh, one more thing").

### 4.4 Seating
- Don't sit **opposite** (frontal, job-interview energy, only a hand to reach). Sit diagonally or side by side.
- If you are too far apart, say it out loud and move: *"I feel like we're sitting a bit far apart. We've got to know each other a bit better now."* Smile, then change topic. Bolder: pull her chair closer ("come here"), but only after you have opened up and shown real interest, otherwise it reads as possessive. Watch her reaction and back off if it is too much.
- Bar stools: "we're sitting a bit far, come here", and slide her stool closer.

### 4.5 The kiss
- **Timing:** roughly after two thirds of the date, not at the end. A first-date kiss is not a must for everyone, he says in the touch podcast, but in the older "touching" video he calls it a habit: always kiss on first dates, in the second third. For a three-hour date: hour one casual touch, hour two kiss, hour three relaxed (hold hands while walking, talk about anything).
- "There was no right moment" is an excuse, he says: you did not dare. From her side: she chose an outfit and spent hours, and you left her at the door unkissed. Either "poor guy didn't dare" or "I wasn't his type". Women forgive timidity less than feeling unwanted.
- "The perfect moment is a myth; it arises afterwards in her memory. Clumsy is fine, the only thing that counts is that you did it."
- Kiss approaches:
  - *"I have to test one more thing"*, then take her head, look at her lips, pull her in.
  - *The non-kiss:* "I'd like to try something but it's important we don't kiss, okay?" "Give me your hands." Slowly pull her close, repeating "but don't forget, we mustn't kiss." Come so close your lips almost touch, close your eyes; she closes hers. When she kisses you, step back: "hey, you broke the rules."
  - *Name the elephant:* "You know what? This is like one of those moments in the movies where the guy doesn't dare kiss her." One woman answered "then just do it". If she declines: "you're right, that would be way too early."
- **"Say the unspoken thing"** works elsewhere too. Texting: "As much fun as this is, neither of us wants to text back and forth forever. I'll call you later." First approach: "I know it must be strange being spoken to like this, but I just had to say hi."

## 5. Mindset, and what happens after the date

### 5.1 If she goes silent after the date
*Sources: [Der wahre Grund, warum sie nach dem Date schweigt](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=X7o-6JYTSsk), [Funkstille nach dem ersten Date?](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=v1NaQ84u6qY)*

**His claim:** the silence was decided *on the date*, not in the chat. No message wording will fix it. "Stress" is not credible: if she felt something, she would make time for it. The causes he names:
- **No emotional connection.** It stayed informational.
- **Too few women in your life,** so too much pressure on this one, which makes you overthink.
- **You filed down your personality.** No opinion, no edges, no polarity, so no attraction. Owning your flaws ("Laster") makes you more interesting than a list of virtues. *Examples:* one host says openly that social media is his vice; Andy says his is wanting to be the centre of attention, which he hid for years and which killed the energy. Now he is loud on dates, and the women he likes find that attractive.
- **Goal-fixation.** Focus on the process ("only to the next tree"), not the result. Wanting this woman to be "special" instead of "one of many" means you cannot let go.

**What not to do after the date:** the "nice guy" reply ("no worries, tell me if you need anything"), filler like "hope you have a nice day", re-reading the chat, typing and deleting for hours. Each of her terse replies gives a dopamine hit that you read as interest.

**The concrete fix:** more social contact. *Tiny step:* make every conversation five seconds longer; add one extra question when you would normally say goodbye. Then meet more women. He gives no texting script or timing rule.

**The "mental" cause of no second date** (from the Funkstille episode): the *seller position* ("I must convince her, she's doing me a favour, I'm wasting her time"). Silence feels deadly, but a minute of silence enjoying the surroundings is fine. He also says to stop denying your sexual side. His sample wording: *"Yes, of course I'd like to sleep with you, and I want to get to know you as a person. Both, obviously. You're a woman, I'm a man. Why should I be ashamed? Now tell me more about you."*

### 5.2 From date to girlfriend
*Source: [3 Tipps: Vom Date zur Freundin](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=8DR4VGUIP04). This is on Andy's channel but the speaker is guest coach Tim Enevoldsen.*
1. **Don't over-invest early.** Up to sex the man usually invests more (arranging, texting, asking). If you are already totally in love after one meeting and text and call constantly, she feels boxed in or that he "needs it".
2. **Keep meeting other women** while you get to know one. It keeps you independent and protects against infatuation. Only slow down when it is firmly heading where you want.
3. **Focus on fun.** Don't ask "what is this between us?". If she felt pressure, she feels obliged. At some point she will ask, and you just say "I can imagine a relationship". He says it takes from about a month to three or four months.

### 5.3 If she asks what you are looking for
*Source: [NEVER ask these 6 questions, Part 2](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rIe72HD2rcM)*

His model answer when you want a relationship but do not want to commit on date one:

> "I've always wanted a relationship, it's really important to me; I want to marry someday and have kids. But that doesn't mean I buy the cat in the bag. I'm critical and check whether it fits. We're having a great time and I'd like to see you again and see where it goes, but I can't say from one date if we fit."

It signals a clear goal and independence. Don't say "for me only a relationship is an option" on date one (too much pressure). If you want something casual, be honest and playful: *"I'm Disneyland if you want fun; if you want something serious, not me."* Watch for people who mirror you ("I want whatever you want"). Congruence, meaning saying and doing the same, is what is attractive.

### 5.4 Not sleeping with her on the first date
*Source: [Frauen aufs 2. Date bekommen (Nutze DIESEN Satz!)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NL-PSzoAFyo), an older video (2017) from Andy's "Authentic Charisma" brand.*

- He often says early on: **"By the way, we won't sleep together today."** Or: "I still have to work, I can only stay until eleven." If she says "I wasn't planning to", he answers "great, we're on the same page".
- **Why:** forbidden fruit is the most interesting; it takes the pressure off *him* (no "do I have to perform?"); and it puts him in the lead ("I decide how fast this goes"). Women usually do not mind sex, they mind pressure.
- **The effect he claims:** she often texts "when do we see each other again?" because she cannot put him in a box ("he loves me, he loves me not"). He becomes a bit of a mystery.
- He also recommends a rising trajectory across dates: date 1 lots of touch, maybe a small kiss at the end; date 2 a kiss or more; date 3 more intimate topics (love, romance, past relationships). Neither side should feel the dates are "going nowhere".
- He caveats that if you both really want it, he is "the last one to tell you not to".

## 6. Your two questions: what he actually says

### "Don't ask for a second date right away"
**Not found as a rule in any of the 13 videos.** What comes closest:
- **The 2017 video (section 5.4)** is titled "Getting her to a second date". His approach is to make *her* ask: set a time limit and say "we won't sleep together today", so she cannot categorise you and writes "when do we see each other again?". He does not say "never ask for a second date", but he clearly prefers that the interest comes from her side.
- **The Tim Enevoldsen video (section 5.2)** advises against pushing for commitment and relationship talk, not against arranging the next date.
- **The elephant technique (section 4.5)** goes the other way on texting: don't ping-pong messages, say "I'll call you later" and move to a real call.
- **The Funkstille and silence episodes (section 5.1)** treat "she doesn't reply to 'shall we meet again?'" only as a symptom, and give no script for asking.

So if you heard "don't ask right away" somewhere, it is either in another video I did not find, or it is the "make her ask" idea from the 2017 video. Tell me the video and I will check.

### "The hand test"
**There is no video that calls it that, but there are three related pieces:**
- **Brief hand-hold as a probe** ([Körperkontakt beim Date](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=C5m_F1oojBs)). Andy says he would always try to hold hands briefly on a first date "to see whether she is someone who likes it or not". If it is too much for her, you let go and say *"oh, all good, no problem"*. That also shows you do not pressure her. His partner disagrees a little: many women find hand-holding at a first date too intimate, because for her it signals a relationship. Rule: if she pulls back, stop.
- **The hand-size game** ([Funkstille nach dem ersten Date?](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=v1NaQ84u6qY)). If you have talked for an hour, are walking side by side and still have not taken her hand, that is fear. Playful method: *"Show me your hand, I want to see whose is bigger"*, then take it. She knows what is going on, but it is light and funny.
- **Hand while speaking** ([Frauen richtig anfassen](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mHsB9-T-0qU)). Take her hand while saying something else ("with some people I can't open up so fast, but with you I feel I can"), so the touch is not the focus.

Your "hold her hand for a bit and see how she reacts" reading is close to the first one.

## 7. Quick checklist

**Before**
- Pick a walk or an activity, not a restaurant or cinema. Plan a start point and a rough route.
- Decide you are fine paying a small amount (ice cream, a drink) and not more.

**During**
- Within the first minutes, ask permission for a personal question, then ask something deep (clone question, last time she cried).
- Probe every answer ("give me an example"). Don't stay at facts.
- Try the question game; ask "do you find me attractive?" after a few rounds.
- Touch early and lightly, while talking. If she flinches, stop.
- Try a brief hand-hold; if not welcome, "all good, no problem".
- Sit diagonally or side by side. If too far, say so and move closer.
- Kiss in the second third of the date, not at the goodbye.
- Be honest about what you are looking for, with a clear long-term goal and no pressure. Ask about her exes, money, kids and how she handles disagreement across the first three dates.

**After**
- Don't chase with filler messages or the "no worries, take your time" reply.
- Don't ask "what is this between us"; keep it fun.
- If you get silence, the fix is upstream: more women in your life, more real connection on the next date.
